answer.short_answer: Ji haan, agar kisi agreement ka consideration ya object unlawful ho to woh agreement void hota hai.
answer.explanation: Contract Act, 1872 ke mutabiq, har woh agreement jiska consideration ya object unlawful ho, void qarar diya jata hai.

citations.quote: Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.
Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found

Yes, you may demand the return of a gratuitously lent item at any time, but you must indemnify the borrower if the premature return causes them a loss that exceeds the benefit they derived from the loan.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, a lender can reclaim a gratuitously lent item even before the agreed time or purpose is fulfilled. However, if the borrower has acted in reliance on the loan such that the early return causes them a loss greater than the benefit they received, the lender is legally required to compensate the borrower for that excess loss.

citations.quote: The lender of a thing for use may at any time require its return, if the loan was gratuitous, even though he lent it for a specified time or purpose. But, if, on the faith of such loan made for a specified time or purpose, the borrower has acted in such a manner that the return of the thing lent before the time agreed upon would cause him loss exceeding the benefit actually derived by him from the loan, the lender must, if he compels the return, indemnify the borrower for the amount in which the loss so occasioned exceeds the benefit so derived.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
جی ہاں، عدالت معاہدے میں طے شدہ جرمانے کی رقم سے زیادہ رقم دلانے کا اختیار رکھتی ہے۔
answer.explanation: مخصوص دادرسی ایکٹ کے تحت، اگر کسی معاہدے میں خلاف ورزی کی صورت میں کوئی رقم درج ہو، تو عدالت اس رقم کے باوجود معاہدے کی مخصوص تعمیل کروا سکتی ہے اور نقصان کے ازالے کے لیے مناسب رقم کا تعین کر سکتی ہے۔

citations.quote: وہ معاہدہ جو بصورت دیگر مخصوص نفاذ کے لیے مناسب ہو اسے نافذ کیا جا سکتا ہے، اگر چہ اس میں رقم درج ہو جو خلاف ورزی پر ادا کی جانی ہے، اور نادہندہ فریق اسے ادا کرنے پر راضی ہو۔

answer.short_answer: No, you are not entitled to hold them liable; in fact, you may be liable to compensate them for any loss caused by your failure to provide the necessary requirements.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, if one party prevents the other from performing their promise, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the prevented party, who is then entitled to compensation for any loss sustained. Furthermore, if a contract consists of reciprocal promises and the party responsible for the first step fails to perform it, they cannot claim the performance of the other party and must compensate them for any resulting loss.

citations.quote: When a contract contains reciprocal promises, and one party to the contract prevents the other from performing his promise, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party so prevented; and he is entitled to compensation from the other party for any loss which he may sustain in consequence of the non-performance of the contract.

When a contract consists of reciprocal promises, such that one of them cannot be performed, or that its performance cannot be claimed till the other has been performed, and the promisor of the promise last mentioned fails to perform it, such promisor cannot claim the performance of the reciprocal promise, and must make compensation to the other party to the contract for any loss which such other party may sustain by the non-performance of the contract.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, agar debtor ne payment ki mad wazeh na ki ho, to creditor apni marzi se usay kisi bhi qanooni udhaar par adjust kar sakta hai, chahay wo time-barred hi kyun na ho.
answer.explanation: Contract Act ki Section 60 ke mutabiq, agar debtor ne ye na bataya ho ke payment kis udhaar ke liye hai aur koi aur halaat bhi is ki nishandahi na karte hon, to creditor ko ikhtiyar hasil hai ke wo us payment ko kisi bhi aise qanooni udhaar par adjust kar le jo us waqt debtor par wajib-ul-ada ho, khwah us udhaar ki wasooli par qanoon-e-me'ad (limitation of suits) ka اطلاق hota ho ya na ho.

citations.quote: Where the debtor has omitted to intimate and there are no other circumstances indicating to which debt the payment is to be applied, the creditor may apply it at his discretion to any lawful debt actually due and payable to him from the debtor, whether its recovery is or is not barred by the law in force for the time being as to the limitation of suits.

answer.short_answer: Agar contract mein performance ki jagah fix nahi hai aur promisee ki taraf se koi application nahi di gayi, toh promisor ka farz hai ke woh promisee se performance ke liye ek munasib jagah muqarrar karne ki darkhwast kare.
answer.explanation: Contract Act ke mutabiq, jab performance ke liye koi jagah tay na ho aur promisee ki taraf se koi application na di gayi ho, toh promisor ko chahiye ke woh khud promisee se rabta karke jagah tay karwaye aur phir wahan performance mukammal kare.

citations.quote: When a promise is to be performed without application by the promisee, and no place is fixed for the performance of it, it is the duty of the promisor to apply to the promisee to appoint a reasonable place for the performance of the promise, and to perform it at such place.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
In the absence of a contract to the contrary, co-sureties are liable to pay an equal share of the debt or the portion remaining unpaid by the principal debtor.
answer.explanation: The law provides that when multiple individuals act as co-sureties for the same debt, they are responsible for dividing the liability equally among themselves unless they have specifically agreed otherwise.

citations.quote: the co-sureties, in the absence of any contract to the contrary, are liable, as between themselves, to pay each an equal share of the whole debt, or of that part of it which remains unpaid by the principal debtor.

answer.short_answer: عوامی راستے پر لاپرواہی سے گاڑی چلانے کی صورت میں دو سال تک قید، جرمانہ یا دونوں سزائیں ہو سکتی ہیں۔
answer.explanation: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کے مطابق، اگر کوئی شخص عوامی راستے پر اس قدر لاپرواہی یا غفلت سے گاڑی چلاتا ہے کہ جس سے انسانی زندگی کو خطرہ ہو یا کسی دوسرے شخص کو نقصان پہنچنے کا امکان ہو، تو اسے دو سال تک کی قید یا جرمانہ یا دونوں سزائیں دی جا سکتی ہیں۔

citations.quote: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 2[two years] or with fine which may extend to 1[three] thousand rupees, or with both.

answer.short_answer: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کی دفعہ 357 کے تحت کسی شخص کو غلط طریقے سے قید کرنے کی کوشش میں حملہ کرنے یا جبر مجرمانہ استعمال کرنے کی سزا ایک سال تک قید، تین ہزار روپے تک جرمانہ، یا دونوں ہو سکتی ہے۔
answer.explanation: پاکستان پینل کوڈ کی دفعہ 357 کے مطابق، جو کوئی شخص کسی دوسرے شخص کو غلط طریقے سے قید کرنے کی کوشش میں اس پر حملہ کرے یا جبر مجرمانہ استعمال کرے، تو اسے ایک سال تک کی قید یا تین ہزار روپے تک جرمانہ یا دونوں سزائیں دی جا سکتی ہیں۔

citations.quote: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting wrongfully to confine that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to 3[three thousand rupees], or with both.

answer.short_answer: A person who advocates for the abolition of Pakistan's sovereignty may be punished with rigorous imprisonment for up to ten years and is also liable to a fine.
answer.explanation: Under the Pakistan Penal Code, anyone who advocates for the curtailment or abolition of Pakistan's sovereignty, or condemns the creation of Pakistan, with the intent to influence others in a manner prejudicial to the safety or ideology of the country, faces these penal consequences.

citations.quote: advocate the curtailment or abolition of the sovereignty of Pakistan in respect of all or any of the territories lying within its borders, whether by amalgamation with the territories of neighboring States or otherwise, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.

answer.short_answer: Yes, an individual can be charged with cheating by personation even if the person they are pretending to be is imaginary.
answer.explanation: The Pakistan Penal Code explicitly states that the offence of cheating by personation is committed regardless of whether the person being personated is a real or an imaginary person.

citations.quote: The offence is committed whether the in dividual personated is a real or imaginary person.

answer.short_answer: Under Section 337Q of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, the arsh for causing the destruction (itlaf) of an organ found singly in a human body is equivalent to the value of diyat.
answer.explanation: The law specifies that for organs that exist singly in the human body, such as the nose or tongue, the compensation payable as arsh is equal to the full value of diyat.

citations.quote: The arsh for causing itlaf of an organ which is found singly in a human body shall be equivalent to the value of diyat.

answer.short_answer: An intoxicated person who causes annoyance in a public place may be punished with simple imprisonment for up to twenty-four hours, a fine of up to thirty rupees, or both.
answer.explanation: Under Section 510 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, misconduct in a public place by a person in a state of intoxication that causes annoyance to others is a punishable offense.

citations.quote: Whoever, in a state of intoxication appears in any public place, or in any place which it is a trespass in him to enter, and there conducts himself in such a manner as to cause annoyance to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to twenty-four hours, or with fine which may extend to 1[thirty] rupees, or with both.

answer.short_answer: The maximum term of imprisonment for causing mudihah to another person is five years.
answer.explanation: Under Section 337F of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, an individual who causes mudihah to another person is liable to daman and may be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term extending up to five years as ta'zir.

citations.quote: (iv) mudihah to any person, shall be liable to daman and may also be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years as ta'zir

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, agar koi shakhs bad-diyanti ya fareb se kisi qarz ya demand ko qanooni taur par adaigi ke liye dastiyab hone se rokta hai, to usay saza ho sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Pakistan Penal Code ke mutabiq, jo shakhs apne ya kisi aur ke qarz ki adaigi ke liye kisi debt ya demand ko qanooni taur par available hone se rokta hai, usay do saal tak ki qaid, jurmana, ya dono sazaein di ja sakti hain.

citations.quote: Whoever dishonestly or fraudulently prevents any debt or demand due to himself or to any other person from being made available according to law for payment of his debts or the debts of such other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
Yes, it is a criminal offense to accept gratification as a motive or reward for inducing a public servant to perform or forbear from an official act through the exercise of personal influence.
answer.explanation: Under the Pakistan Penal Code, any person who accepts, obtains, or attempts to obtain gratification for themselves or others as a reward for using personal influence to induce a public servant to perform or refrain from an official act is subject to punishment, which may include imprisonment for up to one year, a fine, or both.

citations.quote: Whoever accepts or obtains, or agrees to accept or attempts to obtain, from any person, for himself or for any other person, any gratification whatever, as a motive or reward for in ducing, by the exercise of personal influence, any public servant to do or to forbear to do any official act... shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, National Assembly ke dissolve hone ki surat mein Federal Government Federal Consolidated Fund se kharchon ke liye funds authorize kar sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Aaeen ke mutabiq, jab National Assembly dissolve ho jaye to Federal Government kisi bhi maali saal mein char mah se zyada arsay ke liye estimated expenditure authorize kar sakti hai, jab tak ke Article 82 ke tehat grants ki voting aur schedule ki tasdeeq ka amal mukammal na ho jaye.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: at any time when the National Assembly stands dissolved, the Federal Government may authorize expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund in respect of the estimated expenditure for a period not exceeding four months in any financial year

answer.short_answer: If a member of a Provincial Assembly is appointed as Governor, their seat in the Assembly becomes vacant on the day they enter upon their office.
answer.explanation: According to the Constitution, a Governor cannot be a member of a Provincial Assembly, and the seat of any such member appointed as Governor is vacated upon the commencement of their term in the Governor's office.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: if a member of 1[Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)] or a Provincial Assembly is appointed as Governor, his seat in 1[Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)] or, as the case may be, the Provincial Assembly shall become vacant on the day he enters upon his office.

answer.short_answer: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 ke Article 203F ke tehat, Federation ya Province ke liye appeal karne ki muddat faislay ke baad chhay (6) mahine hai.
answer.explanation: Article 203F(1) ke mutabiq, aam taur par appeal 60 din mein ki ja sakti hai, lekin Federation ya Province ke liye yeh muddat barha kar chhay mahine kar di gayi hai.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: Provided that an appeal on behalf of the Federation or of a Province may be preferred within six months of such decision.

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
No, a court cannot validate an act of high treason against the Constitution.
answer.explanation: The Constitution explicitly prohibits any court, including the Federal Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court, and any High Court, from validating acts of high treason as defined in Article 6.

citations.act_or_case: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
citations.quote: An act of high treason mentioned in clause (1) or clause (2) shall not be validated by any court including the Federal Constitutional Court, Supreme Court and a High Court.

Ji haan, Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ki Section 39(2) ke tehat court khud se (of its own motion) kisi decree ko execution ke liye kisi subordinate court ko transfer kar sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Section 39(2) wazeh taur par bayan karti hai ke jis court ne decree pass ki ho, woh apni marzi se (suo motu) ise kisi aisi subordinate court ko bhej sakti hai jo is mamlay mein jurisdiction rakhti ho.

citations.quote: The Court which passed a decree may of its own motion send it for execution to any subordinate Court of competent jurisdiction.

answer.short_answer: No, a public officer cannot be arrested or have their property attached in a suit regarding their official duties, except in the execution of a decree.
answer.explanation: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a public officer is protected from arrest and the attachment of their property during a lawsuit concerning acts performed in their official capacity, unless it is specifically for the execution of a decree.

citations.quote: In a suit instituted against a public officer in respect of any act purporting to be done by him in his official capacity__ (a) the defendant shall not be liable to arrest nor his property to attachment otherwise than in execution of a decree

جی ہاں، کوڈ آف سول پروسیجر 1908 کی سیکشن 86A کے تحت مخصوص حالات میں سفارتی نمائندے کے خلاف قانونی کارروائی کی جا سکتی ہے۔
answer.explanation: سفارتی نمائندے کے خلاف کارروائی تب ممکن ہے جب معاملہ نجی غیر منقولہ جائیداد، وراثت (بطور نجی فرد)، یا پاکستان میں کسی پیشہ ورانہ یا تجارتی سرگرمی سے متعلق ہو۔ اس کے علاوہ، اگر سفارتی نمائندہ خود کوئی کارروائی شروع کرے تو وہ جوابی دعویٰ (counter-claim) سے استثنیٰ کا دعویٰ نہیں کر سکتا، اور متعلقہ ریاست استثنیٰ سے دستبردار بھی ہو سکتی ہے۔

citations.quote: No proceeding in any Court shall lie against a diplomatic agent except in a case relating to__ (a) any private immoveable property situated in Pakistan held by him in his private capacity and not on behalf of the sending State for the purpose of the mission ; (b) a succession in which the diplomatic agent is involved as executor, administrator, heir or legatee as a private person and not on behalf of the sending State; (c) any professional or commercial activity exercised by the diplomatic agent in Pakistan outside his official functions.

The initiation of any proceedings in a Court by a diplomatic agent shall preclude him from invoking immunity from jurisdiction under this section in respect of any counter-claim directly connected with the principal claim. (4) The immunity of a diplomatic agent under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) may be waived by the sending State; and any such waiver shall be express.

answer.short_answer: Yes, a High Court may order the execution of a decree before the costs are ascertained, excluding the portion related to costs.
answer.explanation: If a High Court deems it necessary, it can order the immediate execution of a decree passed in its original civil jurisdiction before costs are taxed, provided that the execution does not include the costs until they are ascertained.

citations.quote: Where any 3* High Court considers it necessary that a decree passed in the exercise of its original civil jurisdiction should be executed before the amount of the costs incurred in the suit can be ascertained by taxation, the Court may order that the decree shall be executed forthwith, except as to so much thereof as relates to the costs

answer.short_answer: Yes, the court has the discretion to allow you to pay the deficient court fees at any stage of the proceedings.
answer.explanation: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, if the required court fees for a document have not been paid, the court may permit the person responsible to pay the amount at any stage. Once paid, the document is treated as if the fees had been paid initially.

citations.quote: Where the whole or any part of any fee prescribed for any document by the law for the time being in force relating to court-fees has not been paid, the Court may, in its discretion, at any stage, allow the person, by whom such fee is payable, to pay the whole or part, as the case may be, of such court-fee; and upon such payment the document, in respect of which such fee is payable, shall have the same force and effect as if such fee had been paid in the first instance.

answer.short_answer: Income derived from a business or source that has ceased is treated as if the business or source had not ceased at the time the income was derived, provided that such income would have been chargeable to tax under the Ordinance had it been derived before the cessation.
answer.explanation: Under Section 72, if income is received from a source that has ceased either before or during the tax year, the Ordinance applies to that income as if the source were still active, assuming the income would have been taxable under the Ordinance prior to the cessation.

citations.quote: this Ordinance shall apply to the income on the basis that the business, activity, investment or other source had not ceased at the time the income was derived.

answer.short_answer: No, two individuals cannot be considered associates solely because they are both employees of the same company.
answer.explanation: The Income Tax Ordinance explicitly states that the status of being associates does not arise merely from the fact that two persons are employees of the same employer.

citations.quote: Two persons shall not be associates solely by reason of the fact that one person is an employee of the other or both persons are employees of a third person.

answer.short_answer: No, mutual funds and insurance companies are not subject to the same capital gain tax computation rules under Section 100B as other entities.
answer.explanation: Section 100B explicitly excludes mutual funds and insurance companies from the standard computation and collection rules laid down in the Eighth Schedule. Instead, these entities are required to have their capital gains computed and determined by the NCCPL according to the mechanism prescribed under Section 37A, while continuing to deposit tax as per the applicable provisions of the Ordinance.

citations.quote: The provisions of sub–section (1) shall not apply to the following persons or class of persons, namely:- (a) a mutual fund; banking company and an insurance company subject to tax under the Fourth Schedule

NCCPL, in case of banking company, insurance company and mutual funds, shall compute and determine the capital gain as per the mechanism prescribed under section 37A; however, these entities shall continue to deposit tax on the amount of capital gain as per the applicable provisions of this Ordinance.

Ji haan, aap police officer par shak ya yaqeen zahir kar sakte hain agar aapko shuba ho ke koi raqam ya jaidad dehshat gardi se hasil ki gayi hai.
answer.explanation: Qanoon ke mutabiq, koi shakhs police officer par shak ya yaqeen zahir kar sakta hai ke koi raqam ya jaidad dehshat gardi se hasil ki gayi hai, ya aisa koi mawad jo shak par mabni ho.

answer.short_answer: A person sentenced by an Anti-terrorism Court must file an appeal to the High Court within fifteen days of the passing of the sentence.
answer.explanation: According to the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, an appeal against a sentence passed by an Anti-terrorism Court may be preferred by the sentenced person to the High Court within a period of fifteen days.

citations.quote: An appeal under sub-section (1) may be preferred by a person sentenced by 1[an Anti- terrorismCourt] to 1[a High Court] within 2[fifteen] days of the passing of the sentence.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 ke tehat adalat insaaf ke taqazon ko pura karne ke liye gawah ki pehchan chupane ki gharz se unki awaaz aur chehre ko badalne (morphing) ka order de sakti hai.
answer.explanation: Adalat yeh order tabhi de sakti hai jab woh mutma'in ho ke yeh gawah ki hifazat, public interest, ya jaldi faislay ke liye zaroori hai, aur is se defendant ko munsifana trial (fair trial) milna mutasir na ho.

citations.quote: The Court in furtherance of the interest of justice may order the image and voice of the witness to be morphed so as to protect the identity of the same

answer.short_answer: A husband who fails to provide the required written notice of a divorce to the Chairman is liable to be punished with simple imprisonment for up to one year, a fine of up to five thousand rupees, or both.
answer.explanation: Under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, the failure to comply with the notice requirements stipulated in sub-section (1) of Section 7 constitutes a punishable offense.

citations.quote: Whoever contravenes the provisions of sub-section (1) shall be punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both.

answer.short_answer: If a wife exercises a delegated right to divorce or if parties seek to dissolve a marriage through means other than talaq, the procedural requirements of Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, apply mutatis mutandis.
answer.explanation: The law mandates that for any dissolution of marriage other than talaq, including cases of delegated divorce (talaq-e-tafweez), the same procedural framework established for talaq under Section 7 must be followed with necessary modifications.

citations.quote: Where the right to divorce has been duly delegated to the wife and she wishes to exercise that right, or where any of the parties to a marriage wishes to dissolve the marriage otherwise than by talaq, the provisions of section 7 shall, mutatis mutandis and so far as applicable, apply.

The same procedural framework, with necessary modifications, also applies to the dissolution of marriage otherwise than by talaq, including cases where the husband has delegated the right of divorce to the wife.

answer.short_answer: Agar Union Council ka Chairman non-Muslim ho, toh Arbitration Council apne Muslim members mein se kisi ek ko Chairman muntakhib karegi.
answer.explanation: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance ke tehat, agar Union Council ka Chairman non-Muslim ho, toh Council ke liye lazmi hai ke woh apne Muslim members mein se kisi ek ko is Ordinance ke maqasid ke liye Chairman chune.

citations.quote: Provided that where the Chairman of the Union Council is a non- Muslim, or he himself wishes to make an application to the Arbitration Council, or is, owing to illness or any other reason, unable to discharge the functions of Chairman, the Council shall elect one of its Muslim members as Chairman for the purposes of this Ordinance

answer.short_answer: No sufficient source found
If immediate action is required, an investigating officer may conduct a search and seizure with the prior permission of a senior officer of the concerned agency who is not below the rank of BS-20.
answer.explanation: While the general rule requires prior permission from the Court for search and seizure, the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010 provides a specific proviso for situations where immediate action is necessary, allowing authorization from a senior officer of at least BS-20 rank instead.

citations.quote: Provided that where immediate action is required, the powers of search and seizure shall be exercisable with prior permission of senior officer of the concerned investigating or prosecuting agency not below the rank of an officer of BS-20.

answer.short_answer: Ji haan, BS-17 aur us se upar ke civil servants ki assets ki tafseelat public ke liye available hoti hain.
answer.explanation: Civil Servants Act, 1973 ke mutabiq, BS-17 aur us se upar ke civil servants, unke spouse aur dependent children ki assets ki declaration Federal Board of Revenue ke paas digitally file ki jati hai aur yeh FBR ke zariye public ke liye available hoti hai.

citations.quote: the declaration of assets of a Civil Servant of BS-17 and above, his spouse and dependent children, including domestic and foreign assets and liabilities, as may be prescribed, shall be digitally filed with the Federal Board of Revenue and same shall be publicly available, through Federal Board of Revenue, in accordance with the rules as may be prescribed

answer.short_answer: Agar kisi civil servant ki post khatam ho jaye ya cadre mein posts kam ho jayein, toh aam taur par us civil servant ki naukri khatam ki jayegi jo us cadre ya service mein sab se junior ho.
answer.explanation: Civil Servants Act, 1973 ke mutabiq, jab kisi post ke khatam hone ya cadre/service mein posts ki tadaad kam hone ki wajah se kisi civil servant ki naukri khatam karna zaroori ho, toh aam taur par sab se junior shakhs ki naukri khatam ki jati hai.

citations.quote: Where, on the abolition of a post or reduction in the number of posts in a cadre or service, the services of a civil servant are required to be terminated, the person whose services are terminated shall ordinarily be the one who is the most junior in such cadre or service.

answer.short_answer: Federal Board of Revenue Act, 2007, Section 19 ke tehat, Board taxpayers ke liye behtar sahuliyat faraham karne, akhrajat ki wasooli, aur public-private partnership ke tehat fiscal laws se mutaliq khidmat faraham karne ke liye fees ya charges laga sakta hai.
answer.explanation: Section 19 Board ko ikhtiyar deta hai ke woh taxpayers ko behtar sahuliyat dene, direct cost reimbursement, aur investment par munasib munafa hasil karne ke liye fees ya charges lagaye, khas tor par jab khidmat public-private partnership ke zariye di ja rahi hon.

citations.quote: The Board may levy any fee or charges for making expenditure on the provision of enhanced facilities for the taxpayers, or direct cost reimbursement of expenses, and reasonable return on investment or profit; where services are provided in the matters relating to or under any fiscal law under public-private partnership.

answer.short_answer: The Appellate Authority is required to pass appropriate orders on an employee's appeal within ninety days of receiving the application.
answer.explanation: Under the National Command Authority Act, 2010, an aggrieved employee may file an appeal regarding their terms and conditions of service, and the Appellate Authority must decide the matter within a ninety-day timeframe.

citations.quote: The Appellate Authority may provide personal hearing to the applicant and pass appropriate orders within ninety days of the receipt of application.

answer.short_answer: The Provincial Government argued that the 2001 Ordinance redefined "licensee" to include persons generating electricity for self-use with generators over 500 KW, thereby making them liable for electricity duty and withdrawing any previous exemptions.
answer.explanation: The Provincial Government contended that the 2001 Ordinance fundamentally changed the legal position by substituting the definition of "licensee." Consequently, entities using generators over 500 KW for self-use became statutory licensees, rendering them liable to pay electricity duty under section 13 and nullifying the protection previously granted by the 1985 notification.

citations.act_or_case: Govt. of Punjab v. M/s. Kunjah Textile Mills Ltd. & others
citations.quote: The case of the appellant Provincial Government, in a nutshell, is that up to 2001 the respondents may have been entitled to the benefit of the 1985 notification but thereafter the position changed fundamentally on account of the new definition of “licensee” substituted by the 2001 Ordinance. In terms of the last portion thereof (“any person generating the electric power from a generator having the capacity of more than five hundred kilowatt for self use”) they statutorily became licensees. Any protection that they may have had in terms of the 1985 notification stood withdrawn by the 2001 notification and thus they were liable to pay the electricity duty imposed by s. 13.

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne Khyber Girls Medical College ke do doctors ko apni promotion ke liye nayi darkhwastain jama karwane ki hidayat ki hai.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne faisla diya hai ke mutaliqa doctors apni promotion ke liye nayi darkhwastain jama karwayain, jinhein Dean, Khyber Girls Medical College foran IPC ko aglay ijlas mein ghor ke liye bhej denge aur faislay se doctors ko aagah karenge.

citations.quote: On submission of fresh applications for promotion, the Dean of Khyber Girls Medical College Pakistan on receiving the applications, immediately forward the dossier for promotion to the IPC for consideration in the next meeting and communicate the decision to both the aforesaid doctors.

No, a party cannot introduce a new argument or set up a new case for the first time before the Supreme Court if it was not raised in the original pleadings or before the trial court.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court has established that parties are prohibited from raising new contentions at the appellate stage that were not pleaded, framed as issues, or supported by evidence in the trial court, particularly when such arguments require factual inquiry.

citations.act_or_case: Anwar Ali Shah and others v. Sadiq Ali Shah and others
citations.quote: It is, by now, settled that no party can be permitted to set up a new case for the first time before this Court, particularly one requiring factual inquiry. Equally settled is the principle that evidence beyond pleadings is of no legal consequence, and no finding can be founded on a case never pleaded.

When a court dismisses a pre-arrest bail application, police authorities are legally obligated to implement the refusal of bail promptly and in good faith by executing the arrest of the accused.
answer.explanation: The dismissal of a pre-arrest bail application signifies that the court has determined the arrest is lawful and necessary for an effective investigation. Police authorities must not treat the mere filing of a subsequent petition as a stay of arrest; they are required to enforce the judicial order unless an express injunctive or restraining order is granted by a competent court.

citations.act_or_case: Zahid Khan, etc v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another
citations.quote: Absent such an order, a refusal of bail remains fully operative and must be implemented promptly and in good faith by investigating authorities.

citations.act_or_case: Zahid Khan, etc v. The State through Prosecutor General, Punjab and another
citations.quote: He unequivocally affirmed the legal position set out above, confirming that unless there exists an express injunctive or restraining order from this Court, the mere pendency of a petition before the Supreme Court ought not to be treated as a shield by any accused to avoid arrest.

answer.short_answer: The Court must be satisfied that the defendant is avoiding service or that the summons cannot be served in the ordinary way.
answer.explanation: Before ordering substituted service, the Court must have reason to believe that the defendant is intentionally keeping out of the way to avoid service, or that there is some other reason why ordinary service is not possible.

citations.quote: Where the Court is satisfied that there is reason to believe that the defendant is keeping out of the way for the purpose of avoiding service, or that for any other reason the summons cannot be served in the ordinary way, the Court shall order for service of summons

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court held that a cheque payment alone is not conclusive proof of a valid sale transaction in the absence of an agreement to sell or other independent corroborative evidence.
answer.explanation: The Court ruled that merely producing evidence of payment does not satisfy the legal standard required to validate the transfer of immovable property by an attorney to their sons, especially when there is no evidence of a lawful bargain or the principal's prior consent.

citations.act_or_case: Javed Iqbal & others v. Mst. Farhat Iqbal (deceased) through LRs
citations.quote: The alleged payment through cheque, made by the appellant (brother) in favour of the respondent (sister), is not conclusive proof of a valid sale transaction, particularly in the absence of any agreement to sell or other independent corroborative evidence reflecting a lawful bargain. Mere production of such payment, without establishing the underlying transaction, does not satisfy the legal standard required to validate an alienation of immovable property.

answer.short_answer: Under the 2001 Ordinance, a failure to collect required advance tax makes a person a deemed taxpayer in default, which triggers Section 161 and subjects them to severely adverse penal consequences.
answer.explanation: According to the Department's position, if a person required to collect advance tax fails to do so, Section 161 of the 2001 Ordinance is triggered, rendering them a deemed taxpayer in default and activating Section 163, which treats the uncollected amount as tax due under an assessment order.

citations.quote: This alleged failure, according to the Department, triggered s. 161 of the 2001 Ordinance which, inter alia, applies when a person who is required to deduct or collect advance tax fails to do so. Such failure makes that person a deemed taxpayer in default and, inter alia, activates s. 163 which provides as follows: “The provisions of this Ordinance shall apply to any amount required to be paid to the Commissioner under this Division as if it were tax due under an assessment order”.

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court ruled that the forfeiture of the performance guarantee by the Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) was justified and set aside the lower courts' judgments that had ordered its refund.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court determined that the forfeiture of the performance guarantee was reasonable under the circumstances of the case. Consequently, it allowed TCP's appeal and overturned the previous decisions of the Sindh High Court that had directed the refund of the guarantee.

citations.act_or_case: Trading Corporation of Pakistan v. M/s
citations.quote: The forfeiture of the entire amount of the performance guarantee by TCP was justified and reasonable in the facts and circumstances of the case.

citations.act_or_case: Trading Corporation of Pakistan v. M/s
citations.quote: The judgments of the learned Single Judge and the Division Bench of the Sindh High Court, insofar as they direct refund of the performance guarantee, are hereby set aside.

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne observe kiya ke agar petitioner (baap) ne apni beti ke khilaf maintenance ka suit wapas na liya, toh Court apne faislay par nazar-e-sani (review) karegi.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne note kiya ke petitioner ne apni beti ke khilaf maintenance ka suit is bunyad par file kiya tha ke woh kama rahi hai. Petitioner ke wakeel ne suit wapas lene ka yaqeen dilaya tha, aur Court ne wazeh kiya ke agar aisa na hua toh woh apne faislay par dobara ghor karenge.

citations.act_or_case: Sadiq Subhani v. Sadia Arooj and others
citations.quote: In the event the suit is not withdrawn by the petitioner, this fact would cause us to review our judgment.

answer.short_answer: Infertility is not a valid legal ground to deny a wife her dower or maintenance.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court of Pakistan has explicitly stated that infertility, or the suspicion thereof, cannot be used to challenge a woman's status or to deprive her of her legal entitlements to dower and maintenance, as doing so constitutes an abuse of the legal process and an affront to human dignity.

citations.act_or_case: Saleh Muhammad and another v. Mst. Mehnaz Begum and others
citations.quote: However, it must be acknowledged without equivocation that infertility, even if present, is no ground to deny a woman her dower or maintenance.

answer.short_answer: Supreme Court ne High Court ke suit decree karne ke ikhtiyar ko kharij kar diya aur ise High Court ki jurisdiction se bahar qarar diya.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ne wazeh kiya ke High Court apni constitutional jurisdiction (Article 199) ke tehat Family Court ke ikhtiyarat khud istemal nahi kar sakti aur na hi suit decree kar sakti hai. Is wajah se, High Court ka suit decree karne ka faisla set-aside kar diya gaya aur mamla dobara Family Court ko wapis bhej diya gaya.

citations.quote: However, as regards the decision of the High Court to decree respondent No.1’s suit, the same being beyond the jurisdiction of the High Court, is liable to -: 6 :- be set-aside.
The High Court in exercise of its Constitutional jurisdiction cannot arrogate to itself the powers of a family Court and issue decrees.

answer.short_answer: The primary legal controversy concerns the allocation of reserved seats for women and non-Muslims to political parties in the National and Provincial Assemblies in accordance with Articles 51(6)(d), 51(6)(e), and 106(3)(c) of the Constitution.
answer.explanation: The Supreme Court identified that the core issue involves determining how these reserved seats should be allocated to political parties based on their numerical strength in the respective houses, particularly in light of the principle of proportional representation and the constitutional requirements for such allocations.

citations.quote: The core controversy requiring resolution relates to the allocation of reserved seats for women and non-Muslims to political parties in the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies in accordance with Article 51(6)(d) and (e) and Article 106(3)(c) of the Constitution, respectively.

answer.short_answer: The Supreme Court converted the civil petitions into appeals, allowed them, set aside the Tribunal's judgment, and restored the petitioners' seniority to its original condition.
answer.explanation: In the case of Sahibzada Hassan Ali and others v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the Supreme Court determined that the petitioners had made a case for interference, leading the Court to overturn the Tribunal's decision and restore the seniority status of the employees.

citations.quote: As a consequence thereof, we convert these civil petitions into appeals and allow them. Consequently, the impugned judgment of the learned Tribunal is set aside and the seniority of the petitioners is restored to its original condition.

answer.short_answer: High Court of Sindh ki judgment dated November 7, 2024, mein lawyers ki janib se apne clients ke khilaf FIRs darj karwane ke trend ki nishandahi ki gayi hai.
answer.explanation: Supreme Court ke mutabiq, High Court of Sindh ki is judgment mein un cases ki tafseelat di gayi hain jo lawyers ne apne clients ke khilaf darj karwaye hain, jise Court ne ek ahem aur tawajo talab pehlu qarar diya hai.

citations.act_or_case: Syed Basit Hyder Taqvi v. The State (CRL.P. 39-K/2025)
citations.quote: The judgment details the cases lodged by the Advocates against their clients, indicating the aforementioned trend. This is a significant development that necessitates immediate attention.

answer.short_answer: The application for a medical board was initially dismissed by the Area Magistrate, but the decision was later overturned by the Additional Sessions Judge, whose order was subsequently set aside by the Lahore High Court.
answer.explanation: The accused, Allah Yar, filed an application for a medical board before the Area Magistrate, which was dismissed on 21.05.2026. He then filed a revision petition, which the Additional Sessions Judge allowed on 15.06.2026. The High Court later set aside this order, ruling that the Magistrate acted as a persona designata and the order was not subject to revisional jurisdiction.

citations.quote: Allah Yar (mentioned above) filed application before learned Area Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala for constituting medical board... which was dismissed vide order dated: 21.05.2026... Allah Yar (mentioned above) filed revision petition against aforesaid order... which was allowed vide order dated: 15.06.2026 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala

Admittedly, while conducting proceedings on an application seeking medical re-examination of an injured, the Magistrate does not act as a Criminal Court but in the capacity of a persona designata. Consequently, the order dated: 21.05.2026 passed by learned Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala was administrative/ executive in nature and, therefore, was not amenable to revisional jurisdiction... Resultantly, the instant criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed and impugned order dated 15.06.2026 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala is hereby set aside.

answer.short_answer: Lahore High Court ne acquired land ka compensation 5,00,000/- rupay per marla ke uniform rate par tay kiya.
answer.explanation: Court ne yeh faisla land ki location, potential, prevailing market conditions aur judicial precedents ko madd-e-nazar rakhte hue kiya, kyunke nichli adalat aur Land Acquisition Collector ne land ki sahi market value ka andaza nahi lagaya tha.

citations.quote: Keeping in view the totality of circumstances, the location and potential of the acquired land, the prevailing market conditions at the relevant time and the judicial precedents referred to hereinabove, we are of the considered opinion that the ends of justice would be adequately met by assessing the entire land at a uniform rate of Rs.5,00,000/- per marla.

answer.short_answer: The Lahore High Court suggested allowing the petitioner to withdraw the suit and file a fresh one on the same cause of action by impleading the necessary parties.
answer.explanation: The Court determined that when necessary parties are missing, the appropriate procedure, agreed upon by both sides, is to permit the withdrawal of the current suit and the filing of a new one to address the defect, with a direction to the trial court to conclude the proceedings expeditiously.

citations.act_or_case: Muhammad Usman v. NADRA through its Chairman, NSRC, Islamabad and 2 others
citations.quote: In view thereof, the alternate procedure available before this Court for reaching just conclusion of the matter would be to allow the petitioner to withdraw the suit and file afresh one on the basis of same cause of action by impleading necessary parties referred to in the judgments passed by the courts below. When confronted, both the sides have no objection to the said course of action.

answer.short_answer: Yes, a person who provides necessaries to someone incapable of contracting is entitled to be reimbursed from that individual's property.
answer.explanation: Under the Contract Act, 1872, if a person who is incapable of entering into a contract, or anyone they are legally bound to support, is supplied with necessaries suited to their condition in life, the supplier has a legal right to be reimbursed from the property of the incapable person.

citations.quote: If a person, incapable of entering into a contract, or any one whom he is legally bound to support, is supplied by another person with necessaries suited to his condition in life, the person who has furnished such supplies is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of such incapable person.

The Lahore High Court allowed the civil revision, set aside the Additional District Judge's judgment dated 16.02.2019, and restored the Trial Court's judgment dated 07.03.2016, which decreed the petitioners' suit for declaration and cancellation of mutations.
answer.explanation: The High Court found that the Additional District Judge's decision to reverse the Trial Court's decree was incorrect. Consequently, it restored the original decree in favor of the petitioners and dismissed the respondent's suit for possession through partition.

citations.act_or_case: Jannat Begum & others v. Province of Punjab through Collector, Gujrat & others

The impugned judgment and decree dated 16.02.2019 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Gujrat, are hereby set aside, and the consolidated judgment and decree dated 07.03.2016 passed by the learned Civil Judge, Gujrat, are restored. Court ne mazeed kaha ke arrear ki raqam 'mad-e-Amanat' samjhi jaye gi aur iska faisla gawahon ki recording ke baad final decision mein hoga.

The amount of arrear shall be treated as mad-e-Amanat and the same be decided at the time of final decision after recording of evidence of the parties.

answer.short_answer: The Lahore High Court set aside the impugned order dated 06.10.2026 regarding the maintainability of the complaint and remanded the matter to the District Consumer Court, Bhakkar, for a fresh decision.
